Stash for backends for data from public repositories

Source: R/MsBackendPublicRepository.R
MsBackendMetaboLightsStash.Rd

Backend classes for public repository mass spectrometry data, such as MsBackendMetaboLights from the MsBackendMetaboLights package can be stored and restored from stash formats extending the MsBackendMzRStash. Backends can be saved with saveMsObject() and restored with readMsObject(). At present only the alabaster-based stash format is supported.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendMetaboLights'
saveObject(x, path, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendMetaboLights,AlabasterParam'
saveMsObject(object, param, ...)

# S4 method for class 'MsBackendMetaboLights,AlabasterParam'
readMsObject(object, param, offline = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

For saveObject(): a MsBackendMetaboLights object.

path

For saveObject() and readObject()

...

Ignored.

object

An MsBackendMetaboLights object.

param

An AlabasterParam object.

offline

For readMsObject() and readObject(): logical(1) if online lookup and synchronization of the mass spectrometry data files should be disabled. Defaults to offline = FALSE. If set to TRUE all mass spectrometry data files need to be already present in the local cache.

Value

readObject() and readMsObject() return a MsBackendMetaboLights backend.

Note

saveMsObject() for MsBackendMetaboLights does not support (and does not require) the consolidate parameter that most other backends implement to create portable stashes. MsBackendMetaboLights backends retrieve and cache the mass spectrometry data files if needed from the public repository and are thus inherently portable.

Alabaster format, AlabasterParam

Calling saveMsObject() on a MsBackendMetaboLights with an AlabasterParam parameter object stores the backend data in a directory specified with parameter path of the parameter object. The stash folder content is identical to the MsBackendMzRStash with only the class definition of the OBJECT file being specific for the stored backend class.

Restoring a MsBackendMetaboLights from the stash folder imports the metadata and, if not available in the local cache, downloads the mass spectrometry data files from the MetaboLights repository. Synchronizing the locally cached data requires an active internet connection, even if no data needs to be downloaded. Setting parameter offline = TRUE avoids the synchronization, but requires the mass spectrometry data files to be present in the local cache.

The alabaster-format stashes can also be created and restored using the saveObject() and readObject() functions.

Author

Johannes Rainer

Examples


library(Spectra)
library(SpectraStash)
library(MsBackendMetaboLights)

## Retrieve mass spectrometry data files matching a specified file pattern
## for the data set MTBLS39 from MetaboLights
s <- Spectra(mtblsId = "MTBLS39", source = MsBackendMetaboLights(),
    filePattern = "73A.cdf")
#> Used data files from the assay's column "Raw Spectral Data File" since none were available in column "Derived Spectral Data File".

## Stash the `Spectra` object to a temporary folder.
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "metabolights_stash")
saveMsObject(s, AlabasterParam(d))

## List the content of the SpectraStash
dir(d)
#> [1] "OBJECT"                        "_environment.json"            
#> [3] "backend"                       "metadata"                     
#> [5] "processing"                    "processing_chunk_size"        
#> [7] "processing_queue_variables"    "spectra_processing_queue.json"

## List the content of the backend stash (located within the *backend*
## sub-folder)
dir(file.path(d, "backend"))
#> [1] "OBJECT"       "spectra_data"

## Restore the `Spectra` object (with the respective backend); using
## `offline = TRUE` to avoid the lookup of the data set on the MetaboLights
## repository - all mass spectrometry data files of the backend must then be
## already present in the local cache.
res <- readMsObject(Spectra(), AlabasterParam(d), offline = TRUE)
res
#> MSn data (Spectra) with 1584 spectra in a MsBackendMetaboLights backend:
#>        msLevel     rtime scanIndex
#>      <integer> <numeric> <integer>
#> 1            1   0.29600         1
#> 2            1   6.13152         2
#> 3            1  11.90310         3
#> 4            1  17.68512         4
#> 5            1  23.46515         5
#> ...        ...       ...       ...
#> 1580         1   2678.10       557
#> 1581         1   2682.73       558
#> 1582         1   2687.36       559
#> 1583         1   2691.96       560
#> 1584         1   2696.59       561
#>  ... 34 more variables/columns.
#> 
#> file(s):
#> MN073A.cdf
#> CS073A.cdf
#> AM073A.cdf
